q: Sur lie aging plus bâtonnage does what chemically?
accept: yeast autolysis mannoproteins texture
lees stirring releases mannoproteins creaminess
ans: Yeast autolysis releases mannoproteins — texture, breadth, oxidative buffering; stirring (bâtonnage) accelerates it
exp: Muscadet, white Burgundy, Champagne — one mechanism, three accents.

q: An estate wants to replant from cuttings of its own old vines rather than order clones. What sanitary problem does that create, and how is it managed?
accept: massal cuttings carry the mother block's viruses so the vines are indexed first and the infected ones discarded
leafroll and fanleaf come with uncertified cuttings so the nursery virus indexes the selection
you index the old vines then propagate only the clean material
a nursery selection gives diversity with certified sanitary status
certified clonal material is virus indexed so massal cuttings must be indexed in the nursery first
ans: Uncertified massal cuttings carry whatever virus load the mother block holds — grapevine fanleaf and the leafroll-associated viruses above all — since the material has been propagated as found, its sanitary status untested; certified clonal material is virus-indexed, and that guarantee is precisely what the estate is giving up. The managed route is an indexed nursery selection: test the candidate old vines, discard the infected, heat- or meristem-treat material worth rescuing, and propagate a diverse but clean population — the old block's genetic spread with certified stock's sanitary status
exp: A clone is not a variety and not a grade of quality — it is one plant's descendants, and what it sells is sanitary certainty and predictability, not flavour. ENTAV-INRA certification and the Dijon clones (113, 114, 115, 777 for Pinot; 76, 95, 96 for Chardonnay) rescued yields in blocks crippled by virus, but a monoclonal planting concentrates risk and flattens ripening. Leafroll is the one to name aloud: it delays ripening and strips sugar and colour, and there is no cure in a vine already in the ground. Burgundy's swing back toward massale is in practice a swing toward indexed nursery selection, which is the only version of it a bank will finance.

q: Name the bacterium normally responsible for malolactic conversion, the chemical change it makes, and why 'conversion' is the better word than 'fermentation'.
accept: oenococcus oeni malic to lactic plus co2 no sugar fermented
oenococcus converts malic acid into lactic acid and carbon dioxide
bacteria decarboxylate malic to lactic not a sugar fermentation
malic acid becomes lactic acid via oenococcus oeni
losing one acid group is why it softens the wine
ans: Oenococcus oeni decarboxylates harsh dicarboxylic L-malic acid into soft monocarboxylic L-lactic acid, releasing CO2 — no sugar is fermented, so it is a bacterial conversion rather than a true fermentation
exp: Losing one carboxyl group is the entire sensory story: half the acid strength, a pH rise of roughly 0.1–0.3, plus diacetyl butter and microbial stability once the malic food source is gone. Because it is bacterial, it is stopped by the things that inhibit bacteria — pH below about 3.1, cold cellars, SO2, lysozyme, sterile filtration — which is how Riesling and most aromatic whites keep their malic bite while red wine essentially always goes through.

q: A deep, fertile site throws shaded, over-vigorous canopies. Name two divided-canopy training systems and say what the division achieves.
accept: scott henry smart dyson lyre geneva double curtain spread the canopy for light
vertical division scott henry horizontal division lyre more sunlit leaf area
divided canopies expose more leaf and fruit to light
geneva double curtain and lyre split the canopy in two
splitting the canopy stops shading on a high vigour site
ans: Scott Henry and Smart-Dyson divide the canopy vertically, training one shoot set downward; Lyre (U) and the Geneva Double Curtain divide it horizontally into two curtains — spreading the same leaf area so more of it is sunlit, opening the fruit zone, and cutting shade-driven herbaceousness
exp: Richard Smart's argument in Sunlight into Wine: on a vigorous site VSP crams too many shoots into one narrow wall, and the interior leaves go from carbon earners to carbon parasites while shaded fruit stays green and low in anthocyanin. Division is the fix of last resort, chosen when you cannot devigour the site by rootstock, cover crop, dry farming or higher planting density. Names worth attaching: Scott Henry of Oregon's Umpqua Valley, and Nelson Shaulis at Cornell's Geneva station for the GDC.

q: Overhead sprinklers protect budding vines from a radiation frost by:
opts: Releasing latent heat as the water freezes on the bud
Washing frost off the swelling buds before sunrise
Coating the bud in a film that resists freezing
Cooling buds so budbreak comes after the frost
exp: Water gives up roughly 334 joules per gram as it turns to ice, and that release holds the bud at 0°C inside its ice shell while the air around it drops well below. Two consequences the exam wants: the sprinklers must run continuously until the ice thaws, because stopping mid-frost makes evaporative cooling worse than doing nothing, and the water demand is enormous. Compare the alternatives — wind machines only work when a genuine inversion layer puts warm air overhead, and heaters or bougies are brute force. Cooling buds so budbreak comes after the frost describes a real technique (spring sprinkling to hold budbreak back), but that is scheduling, not frost-night protection.

q: Tartaric, malic and lactic acids differ in wine how?
accept: tartaric grape main malic apple lactic soft from mlf
tartaric primary malic sharp lactic soft
ans: Tartaric: the grape's stable backbone; malic: sharp, green-apple (reduced in ripening/MLF); lactic: soft, from malolactic conversion
exp: Tartrate crystals ('wine diamonds') are harmless tartaric precipitate.

accept: tannin seed skin maturity vs brix
brown seeds resolved tannins not just sugar
ans: Maturity of skins, seeds and tannins (browning seeds, resolved bitterness) — which may lag sugar in warm climates
exp: Picking on numbers alone gives green tannin at high alcohol.
